best_for: PC gamers who buy on GOG and want cloud saves, one-click updates and a single library that also shows games from other launchers.

points.title: Optional for GOG games
points.text: GOG says Galaxy remains an optional client for GOG.com games, which the store sells DRM-free. The client adds conveniences on top; it is not a lock on what you bought.

points.title: Saves follow you
points.text: Game saves back up to the cloud and sync between your computers, so you can switch PCs or reinstall without losing progress.

points.title: Roll back a bad patch
points.text: If an update breaks a game, Galaxy can restore an earlier version of it, so one bad patch does not keep you from playing.

points.title: One library for many stores
points.text: Official and community-built integrations import your games from other PC and console platforms into one list. How well each works depends on that integration.

points.title: No Linux client
points.text: Galaxy is offered for Windows and macOS only. GOG lists Linux as a store category for games, but there is no Galaxy client for it.

points.title: Install details
points.text: The Windows installer is 32-bit and installs for all users, so it needs administrator rights. The Mac package needs macOS 14 or later, with Intel and Apple silicon builds.

points.title: Downgrades on Windows only
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 48 versions; macOS lists only the current release, so going back there needs another source.
